newsitem.title: USA: UAL's United October load factor rises.
newsitem.headline: UAL's United October load factor rises.

text.p: UAL Corp said systemwide passenger load factor for United Airlines in October was 72.2 percent, up from 70.9 percent a year ago.
United's total revenue passenger miles were 10.04 billion in October, up 4.1 percent from 9.65 billion from a year ago.

"Our year-over-year U.S. domestic traffic growth continues to be strong despite the reinstatement of the excise tax," John Edwardson, president, said in a statement. "This U.S. domestic traffic growth combined with strength in Latin America traffic were the key factors of our overall system improvement compared with October of last year."
Total revenue passenger miles including charter flights were 10.05 billion, up 3.9 percent from 9.68 billion a year ago.
Domestic revenue passenger miles in October rose 5.3 percent to 6.29 billion, up 5.3 percent, while Pacific revenue passenger miles gained 2.8 percent to 2.26 billion.
Atlantic revenue passenger miles dropped 1.8 percent to 1.03 billion. Latin American revenue passenger miles totaled 464.9 million, up 8.2 percent.
Total scheduled available seat miles were 13.91 billion, up 2.2 percent from 13.61 billion.
Total cargo ton miles for the month were 223.6 million, up 11.9 percent from 199.8 million a year ago.
The rise in October passenger load factor reflected a two-point gain in North America to 71.4 percent from 69.4 percent.

Pacific load factor dropped to 71.6 percent from 71.9 percent in October, while Atlantic load factor rose to 82.8 percent from 82.3 percent. Latin American load factor in October rose to 66.8 percent from 63.7.
